seo_title: Cost of Living in Tashkent 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Tashkent per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Visa-free entry for Russians for 60 days, low prices for housing and food, a developed Russian-speaking environment and a rapidly growing IT scene. A good choice for a family relocation.
pros: Visa-free entry for 60 days for Russian citizens
Low prices for rent and groceries alongside quality infrastructure
Russian is everywhere — schools, healthcare, business
A rapidly growing IT industry and state support for the IT Park
A mild winter and a long, warm spring
cons: Very hot dry summers — up to +40°C in July and August
Difficulties with international transfers and payment systems
Smog in the centre and traffic jams at rush hour
Bureaucracy for long-term legalisation is harder than in Georgia

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 60 days without a visa for Russians, the stamp is issued at the border.

visa_steps.title: Registration
visa_steps.description: If you stay more than 15 days — register via e-mehmon.uz or through your landlord.

visa_steps.title: PINFL
visa_steps.description: An equivalent of the tax ID: needed for a bank account, a sole proprietorship, school. Issued at the public services centre in a couple of days.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Kapitalbank, Uzum Bank, Hamkorbank — open accounts with a passport and PINFL.

visa_steps.title: Sole proprietorship or IT Park resident
visa_steps.description: For a long stay — self-employment or registration in the IT Park (tax benefits).

faq.question: Can I work remotely in Tashkent?
faq.answer: Yes, many open a sole proprietorship and work for foreign clients, with a 4% tax.

faq.question: What about payments in Tashkent?
faq.answer: UZCARD/HUMO work locally; for international use it's Visa/MasterCard via Kapitalbank or Uzum.

faq.question: What about the language in Tashkent?
faq.answer: Uzbek is the state language, but almost everyone understands Russian, and in Tashkent it's often the main language.

faq.question: Which districts are good for living in Tashkent?
faq.answer: Mirabad and Yunusabad — modern developments. Chilanzar — older and budget-friendly.

faq.question: Families with children in Tashkent?
faq.answer: Good private Russian-language schools, with prices from 30,000 ₽ per month.

faq.question: What's the climate in Tashkent?
faq.answer: Winter is mild, down to –5°C. Summer is hot and dry, +35–40°C is normal from June to August.

reviews.text: An IT Park resident, 4% tax, home in a modern complex for 60,000 ₽. The summer heat is tough, but otherwise it's the best balance of price and convenience I've found.
We moved with my husband and child: a Russian-language school, decent healthcare, we visit our Uzbek neighbours. Prices are 2 times lower than in Moscow.
